items.title: A Study on Nail Art Works Using Natural Fractal Motifs Based on Generative AI
items.abstract: This study aimed to develop nail art designs inspired by natural fractal motifs and compare the visual expression of DALL·E, Midjourney, and Stable Diffusion. Four natural fractal motifs were selected through a literature review: clouds, lightning, ant nests, and planets. A shared prompt framework incorporating fractal characteristics, formative elements, and nail art design requirements was established. Common English prompts were used as initial inputs for the three models, followed by image refinement using their respective functions. A focus group interview (FGI) with ten nail art professionals and instructors was conducted to examine design suitability and practical applicability. The generated images exhibited differences in composition, color, texture, and detail. FGI participants highlighted Midjourney’s representation of fractal elements, color harmony, texture rendering, and overall design quality. Their feedback informed the selection of Midjourney for physical artwork development. Four nail art works were produced, incorporating randomness and overlapping, nonlinearity and diffusion, irregularity and distortion, and an artistic interpretation of self-similarity and repetition. The visual features of the generated images were adapted to the materials and techniques used in physical production. This study presents a design development process integrating motif analysis, prompt design, image generation, FGI, and physical production. The findings suggest that generative AI can support the exploration of fractal-inspired nail art and offer a foundation for further applications in beauty design and education.

items.title: AI-Based Decision Support for Asset Allocation Management as a Component of Business Models under Market Uncertainty
items.abstract: Objectives The aim of the study was to identify and evaluate the possibilities of using artificial intelligence assistants to support decision-making processes related to asset allocation, treated as an important component of the business model of an enterprise operating under conditions of market uncertainty. Material and methods The study was conducted on the example of three companies from the construction sector listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange: Budimex S.A., Polimex Mostostal S.A., and Mirbud S.A. The analysis covered the years 2020–2024 and was based on two groups of data: annual fundamental indicators and daily closing stock prices. In the fundamental part, return on equity, debt ratio, asset utilization ratio, and the Altman discriminant model were used to construct a synthetic fundamental index. In the market part, daily logarithmic rates of return and the Sharpe ratio were calculated. Results The results indicate that AI assistants can effectively support the analytical process by accelerating calculations and increasing the repeatability of the procedure. At the same time, differences in model performance were observed, indicating the risk of errors in data interpretation. Conclusions The study demonstrates that AI can be a useful tool supporting asset allocation management; however, its effectiveness depends on data quality, the precision of the analytical procedure, and human supervision. The findings highlight the importance of control mechanisms and model triangulation in AI-supported decision-making processes.

items.title: Barriers to Developing a Safety Culture in the Opinion of Occupational Health and Safety Professionals
items.abstract: Objectives Identification of barriers to the development of a safety culture, determining their importance and detecting associations between them. Material and methods First, a critical and comparative literature analysis was used, followed by a quantitative empirical study. The quantitative analysis examined the frequency of occurrence as well as associations and connections between attributes. A survey was conducted on a sample of 105 people. Results It was found that the most common barriers to the implementation of safety culture in the literature are: (1) lack of leadership and commitment of management, (2) lack of commitment and disregard by employees and (3) lack of understanding by employees. On the other hand, practitioners indicated (1) lack of leadership and commitment of management, (2) problems with communication and (3) lack of commitment and disregard by employees as the most important barriers. Therefore, two of the three most important barriers are the same in both cases and concern people: management on the one hand, and employees on the other. Conclusions A characteristic triad of barriers to developing a safety culture has been identified. In this way, a model approach to the problem was proposed. Understanding them and striving to eliminate them will allow for a more effective shaping of this area of organizational culture.

items.title: Bridging Clinical Prediction and Workplace Exposure: A Data-Driven Risk Stratification and Prediction Model for Occupational Respiratory Diseases.
items.abstract: Abstract Occupational respiratory disease (ORD) surveillance remains largely reactive, with diagnosis often occurring only after clinically significant symptoms develop. Existing risk stratification tools are primarily clinically derived and rarely incorporate occupational exposure variables such as exposure intensity, duration, and workplace hazards, limiting early identification of at-risk workers. This review synthesizes current evidence on predictive modelling and risk stratification tools for respiratory diseases, evaluates their applicability to occupational health, and proposes a data-driven framework for proactive risk stratification. A structured literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published between 2021 and 2025. Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) and free-text terms related to occupational respiratory diseases, predictive modelling, prognostic tools, and occupational exposure assessment were combined using Boolean operators. Extracted data included study characteristics, modelling approaches, predictors, and model performance metrics, which were narratively synthesized using thematic mapping. Of 618 records identified, six representative evidence approaches were retained for detailed comparative synthesis. Clinical models such as BODE and DOSE provided useful prognostic information but lacked occupational exposure parameters. Exposure-based approaches showed associations between cumulative exposure and respiratory outcomes, while a meta-analysis of machine-learning models for acute respiratory distress syndrome reported a pooled AUC of 0.7407. Key predictors included age, smoking status, lung function, and exposure-related factors. Current reactive and clinically focused approaches limit effective ORD prevention. Integrating occupational exposure variables into predictive, data-driven risk stratification frameworks is essential for early identification of high-risk workers. The proposed ORDiRS framework represents a step toward proactive occupational health surveillance in industrial settings.

items.title: Co-Creating a Humane Trading Architecture: Enterprise, Innovation and the Bangladesh–European Union Economic Partnership — A Research Paper on Market Measurement, Digital Sovereignty and Phased Integration
items.abstract: Bangladesh's impending transition from least-developed-country status and the initialling of a Framework Agreement on Comprehensive Partnership and Cooperation with the European Union open a structured opportunity to redesign the bilateral economic relationship. This paper develops the concept of a humane trading architecture in which enterprise competitiveness and innovation capacity function as the principal transmission mechanisms between preferential market access and structural transformation. It integrates multidimensional market-measurement tools (the Economic Vulnerability Index and the Environmental Performance Index), mild-form transaction authentication and data validation for small and medium enterprise trade finance, sovereign computational capacity (including a Bangla large language model embedded in digital public infrastructure), and post-quantum readiness for trade finance. Drawing on comparative lessons from the EU–Vietnam Free Trade Agreement and EU–India negotiations, the paper specifies five negotiating redlines, co-creation pathways in food, fuel and finance, and a three-phase roadmap calibrated to the current United Nations graduation schedule and the pending request for a preparatory extension. The resulting framework preserves strategic autonomy while extending economic franchise to domestic firms and workers. Personal academic views only.

items.title: Enabling spatial intelligence in the AEC lifecycle: a framework and review of large language models
items.abstract: Abstract The Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry is undergoing a profound digital transformation driven by the urgent need to integrate fragmented, heterogeneous data into actionable intelligence. This paper provides a systematic review of 76 representative studies to examine how Large Language Models (LLMs) enable spatial intelligence across the entire building lifecycle. A layered spatial intelligence framework is proposed, encompassing the dimensions of design, construction, operation, as well as research and education. The review demonstrates that LLMs are evolving from passive text processors into active cognitive partners capable of semantic interpretation, spatial reasoning, and complex decision-making. Key findings highlight the effectiveness of LLMs in requirement translation, multimodal design generation, regulatory compliance, and lifecycle Building Information Modeling (BIM) integration. Despite these advancements, significant challenges persist regarding spatial reasoning accuracy, the lack of physical embodiment, and institutional data governance. This research outlines a strategic roadmap toward embodied intelligence, AEC-specific world models, and enhanced human-AI collaboration, providing a structured foundation for the advancement of LLM-driven spatial intelligence in professional practice.

items.title: Exploring Healthcare Professionals' Readiness for Artificial Intelligence in a Resource-Limited Health System: Evidence from Bukavu, Democratic Republic of Congo
items.abstract: Introduction: Artificial intelligence (AI) offers opportunities to improve the efficiency of healthcare, but its integration in sub-Saharan Africa faces structural constraints. This exploratory study analyzes the perceptions, expectations, and fears of healthcare professionals in the Ibanda Health Zone (Bukavu, DRC) to document the professional acceptability of these technologies. Methods: The study used a mixed-methods approach: the qualitative exploratory component was based on semi-structured interviews with 11 professionals (physicians, nurses, technicians, managers). The data underwent inductive thematic analysis supplemented by descriptive frequency quantification. Results: Overall attitudes toward AI are favorable, albeit with certain conditions. Despite a predominantly basic or informal understanding of AI (81.8%), perceived benefits include improved diagnostics (72.7%) and data management (63.6%). However, major obstacles persist: lack of formal training (81.8%), internet instability (72.7%), and concerns about the reliability of results (54.5%). AI acceptance is high but conditional, revealing a gap between technological promises and realities on the ground. Training (cited by 90.9% of participants) emerges as the central lever and an ethical prerequisite for safe use. Conclusion : The integration of AI at Ibanda cannot be reduced to a technical issue; it requires strengthening basic infrastructure, a clear regulatory framework, and active involvement of caregivers in the design of tools.

items.title: Generative AI in Managerial Decision-Making: A Systematic Literature Review of Trust, AI Literacy, and Decision Quality
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly entering managerial decision processes, yet evidence remains fragmented regarding when AI-generated advice should be trusted, how managers should evaluate it, and how decision quality should be assessed. This study systematically reviews GenAI-supported managerial decision-making by integrating PRISMA 2020 screening, bibliometric mapping, author-keyword co-occurrence analysis, thematic synthesis, and the Theory–Context–Characteristics–Methodology (TCCM) framework. A Scopus export containing 3,500 records was screened using temporal, language, document-type, topical, and contextual criteria, yielding 99 studies published between 2024 and 2026. The final corpus comprises 342 unique authors across 94 publication sources. Four themes dominate: decision augmentation and analytics; trust, governance, and explainability; human–AI collaboration and capability; and decision quality and organizational outcomes. Trust is more often represented through governance, transparency, explainability, calibration, and human oversight than as an explicitly measured construct, while AI literacy appears explicitly in only one study. Decision quality is likewise rarely conceptualized directly and is commonly proxied by accuracy, efficiency, or predictive performance. The review proposes an integrative model in which GenAI decision-support capabilities influence managerial decision quality through calibrated trust and human–AI collaboration, with AI literacy functioning as a critical capability for verification and appropriate reliance. The study concludes with a TCCM-based research agenda for human-centered GenAI decision research. Keywords: generative AI; managerial decision-making; trust in AI; AI literacy; decision quality

items.title: How much model does warning triage need? A cost-aware comparison from rules to locally run language models
items.abstract: Static analysis tools report far more warnings than developers act on, and machine learning is widely proposed to identify the actionable ones. Published comparisons rarely include a simple label-based reference, and rarely report quality on unseen projects together with compute time. This study compares five levels of model complexity on two open datasets, NASCAR (Java) and AW4C (C): a warning-type prior, a linear model on term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF) features, a frozen code encoder, fine-tuned code encoders, and open-weight large language models (LLMs) run locally. All models were scored on the same 1,000 warnings per dataset and protocol, using the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) with project-level bootstrap intervals. Three findings emerged. First, in the original AW4C release the number of lines in the supplied code context predicted the label with an MCC of 0.91 on unseen projects, and fine-tuned CodeBERT reached 0.81; in a variant rebuilt with a uniform context window, which also differs in composition, the corresponding values were 0.12 and 0.30. Second, on unseen NASCAR projects an advantage of fine-tuned encoders over the warning-type prior was not established: the paired difference in MCC was −0.08 (95% CI −0.21 to 0.02) for CodeBERT. Third, locally run LLMs without task-specific training scored near zero on NASCAR with the default threshold and required about 47 times the mean processing time of a fine-tuned encoder. Model complexity should be assessed against a simple reference under cross-project evaluation.

items.abstract: This study aims to synthesize the relationship between deep learning strategies and students' critical thinking skills within the context of Economics education. Employing a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) methodology, we examined 24 scholarly publications. The synthesis reveals three key findings: (1) a deep learning approach has a significant influence on higher-order thinking skills (HOTS) and critical thinking abilities; however, this relationship is complex and mediated by variables such as epistemological beliefs, perceptions of the learning context, and intrinsic motivation. (2) The adoption of a deep learning approach does not automatically result in high-level critical thinking skills; therefore, such skills require explicit and structured development. (3) Inquiry-based learning strategies, structured collaboration, and the integration of technology as a cognitive scaffold have proven most effective in promoting both aspects synergistically. This study offers practical implications for the design of Economics instruction—specifically regarding the cultivation of deep knowledge and the development of critical thinking skills—within the framework of the Kurikulum Merdeka (Independent Curriculum).

items.title: Relevance and Applicability of the Master of Arts in Educational Management Curriculum to Graduates' Professional Work: Basis for Curriculum Enhancement
items.abstract: Higher education institutions are expected to continuously evaluate graduate programs to ensure that curricular offerings remain relevant, responsive, and aligned with the evolving demands of professional practice. This study assessed the relevance and applicability of the Master of Arts in Educational Management (MAEM) curriculum of Guagua National Colleges to the current professional work of its graduates and identified areas for curriculum enhancement. Using a quantitative descriptive-comparative research design, data were collected from 33 MAEM graduates through a structured survey questionnaire. Descriptive statistics such as frequency, percentage, weighted mean, and ranking were utilized to analyze quantitative data, while thematic analysis was employed to examine graduates' recommendations. Results revealed that most graduates occupy positions closely related to educational leadership and management, with 87.88% indicating that their present work is highly related or related to educational management. The overall relevance and applicability of the curriculum obtained a very high rating (M = 4.69), while the adequacy of competencies developed through the program received a mean rating of 4.67. Human Resource and Organizational Management emerged as the highest-rated competency area (M = 4.76), whereas Problem-Solving and Evidence-Based Decision-Making obtained the lowest mean rating (M = 4.64), though still interpreted as very high. Graduates recommended strengthening content related to digital leadership, educational technology, artificial intelligence, instructional leadership, research utilization, and experiential learning. Based on these findings, a Responsive MAEM Curriculum Enhancement Framework was proposed. The study concludes that the MAEM curriculum remains highly relevant to current professional requirements but should continuously evolve to address emerging educational challenges and technological advancements.

items.title: RFQ-30: A Synthetic Test Suite for Missing and Conflicting Procurement Inputs
items.abstract: Draft technical note and reproducibility package prepared for Arcforth. RFQ-30 contains 30 AI-assisted synthetic procurement intake cases: ten complete, ten incomplete and ten conflicting. Two deterministic extraction baselines were executed. The first-value baseline matches 230/240 annotated fields but releases ten conflicting requests; the duplicate-aware baseline matches 236/240 fields and still releases four prose-conflict cases. These are descriptive results on a constructed fixture, not operational error estimates. The package includes data, reference labels, code, actual per-case outputs, a frozen local protocol, a data card and limitations. No LLM model was evaluated, no human review time was measured, and no client data or outcomes are included. AI assistance was used in authoring and analysis. Independent practitioner review has not occurred. Corporate authorship and the proposed CC BY 4.0 license require owner confirmation before publication. This draft is not peer reviewed.

items.title: Supernetwork Architecture Selection for Deployable Language Models: RAG Assessment of Overhead-Line Insulators on a 2 GB Device for Grid Operator's Maintenance Crews
items.abstract: Transmission system operators inspecting high-voltage insulator strings using inference using drone capture inference in remote locations need a local LLM assistant that is useful only if its answers are hallucination-free, drawn from operator-held documents and never exceeding what a photograph shows. The assistant presented here is built accordingly, a detector turning photographs into fixed-text findings, retrieval covering 3,780 IEC, CIGRE and IEEE passages and 127 engineer-reviewed question-answer pairs, and code-enforced hallucination guards checking every answer. Because everything runs within the memory restrictions of an edge device such as the 2 GB Arduino UNO Q, the language model must fit the device, so a weight-sharing supernetwork is trained once from Llama 3.2 1B and eleven subnetworks varying in size are extracted and distilled from a Qwen3.5-27B teacher, yielding a deployable model family. Which network is selected is decided by a selection rule, evaluation set and GPT-OSS:20B judge, ranking candidates by answer quality under a hallucination guard gate and memory restrictions. All subnetworks keep guard violations at or below 2.8% and answer the field questions on the device without failure at 2.8 W, the service peaking at 1108 to 1258 MB as quality rises along the memory-quality Pareto frontier from 0.73 to 0.91 and the median 704-token answer lengthens from 79 to 134 s. The shipped network is the fastest of the three tied on quality within 1200 MB, at 0.85, 94 s per answer and 1172 MB.

items.title: The Relationships among Intrinsic Motivation, Work Engagement, and Job Burnout among Female Beauty Professionals
items.abstract: This study examined the relationships among intrinsic motivation, work engagement, and job burnout among female beauty professionals, who account for the large majority of the Korean beauty service workforce. Data from 233 respondents were analyzed using SPSS Statistics 27.0. Intrinsic motivation comprised autonomy and competence, work engagement comprised dedication and absorption, and job burnout comprised reduced personal accomplishment and depersonalization. Autonomy and competence both predicted dedication, whereas only competence predicted absorption. Autonomy and dedication reduced both dimensions of burnout, while competence and absorption were associated with higher burnout; since neither showed a significant bivariate correlation with burnout, these coefficients are interpreted as suppression effects that emerge once autonomy and dedication are controlled. These findings indicate that intrinsic motivation does not function as a uniformly protective resource. Discretion over one’s work and a sense of meaning buffer burnout, whereas competence and sustained absorption may impose psychological costs unless workload and recovery time are managed. Beauty service organizations therefore need to expand autonomy and support competency development while regulating workload at the same time. Given the limited explanatory power of the burnout models, future research should incorporate job demands and organizational resources.

items.title: The use of artificial intelligence by academic teachers in Poland
items.abstract: Objectives The study examines the attitudes of Polish academic teachers toward the use of artificial intelligence in teaching and research, with particular emphasis on their experiences, perceived benefits and concerns. Material and methods The research was based on a quantitative survey conducted in the first half of 2025 using an online questionnaire distributed to public and private universities in Poland. A total of 560 academic teachers participated in the study. The survey explored the scope of AI use in teaching and research, self-assessed competences, perceived advantages and risks, willingness to participate in training, and opinions on institutional regulations concerning AI. Results Most respondents declared experience with AI in teaching rather then research, with younger academics being more likely to use such tools. AI was mainly used for creating teaching materials, searching literature, translating texts, editing content, and preparing tests. Respondents identified time savings, reduced language barriers, and support for creativity as the main benefits of AI. Non-users most often pointed to lack of need, distrust of generated content and ethical concerns. Most respondents had not participated in formal AI training, although expressed willingness to attend such courses. Conclusions The findings suggest that AI is becoming an increasingly important element of academic work in Poland, particularly as a tool supporting repetitive and time-consuming tasks. However, its broader implementation remains limited by insufficient competences, ethical concerns, legal uncertainties, and distrust of AI-generated content.

items.title: "Uso de Tecnologías de la Información y la Comunicación (TIC) y su Asociación con las Dimensiones del Pensamiento Crítico en Discentes de Educación Superior: Un Estudio Mixto Explicativo"
items.abstract: Título: Uso de Tecnologías de la Información y la Comunicación (TIC) y su Asociación con las Dimensiones del Pensamiento Crítico en Discentes de Educación Superior: Un Estudio Mixto Explicativo Antecedentes: En la era digital, la omnipresencia de las Tecnologías de la Información y la Comunicación (TIC) y la irrupción de la Inteligencia Artificial Generativa (IAGen) han transformado los entornos de aprendizaje en salud. En el Internado Rotatorio de Pregrado, el personal médico en adiestramiento enfrenta una constante sobrecarga informativa (infoxicación) e interacción con herramientas automatizadas. Un uso puramente instrumental o delegativo de las TIC puede comprometer el desarrollo de competencias cognitivas de orden superior, mientras que un uso epistémico puede potenciar el análisis, la inferencia, la evaluación y la autorregulación clínica. Objetivo: Determinar la asociación entre los patrones de uso de las TIC (incluyendo la IAGen y la alfabetización informacional) y el nivel de desarrollo de las dimensiones del pensamiento crítico en Médicos Internos de Pregrado (MIP) en unidades de segundo nivel de atención del IMSS, e interpretar los procesos metacognitivos subyacentes desde la perspectiva estudiantil. Material y Métodos: Estudio mixto con Diseño Secuencial Explicativo (DEXPLI). · Fase 1 (Cuantitativa): Diseño multicéntrico, observacional, transversal y analítico en tres sedes (HGZ No. 53, HGZ No. 197 y HGZ No. 71, OOAD Estado de México Oriente). Se incluirá por censo a la plantilla total de MIP. Se aplicará la Escala Multidimensional de Patrones de Uso de TIC (\alpha = 0.87) y un cuestionario estandarizado de dimensiones de Pensamiento Crítico (Facione). Se realizarán análisis descriptivos, correlación de Pearson, ANOVA multicéntrico y modelos de Regresión Lineal Múltiple. · Fase 2 (Cualitativa): Abordaje fenomenológico interpretativo mediante 4 grupos focales (n = 32 MIP) estructurados por muestreo intencional de casos extremos según los cuartiles de desempeño de la Fase 1 (Q_1 y Q_4). Los testimonios serán transcritos y analizados categorialmente mediante codificación temática en ATLAS.ti para triangular las meta-inferencias. Resultados Esperados: Se prevé identificar una asociación positiva y estadísticamente significativa entre el uso epistémico de TIC/IAGen y puntajes elevados en las dimensiones de análisis, inferencia y autorregulación. Asimismo, se espera caracterizar cómo la delegación cognitiva pasiva se vincula con un menor rendimiento crítico y cómo la alfabetización informacional mitiga la infoxicación en la toma de decisiones clínicas. Conclusiones: La investigación aportará evidencia empírica clave para la optimización tecno-pedagógica de los planes de estudio del Internado Rotatorio, permitiendo establecer lineamientos éticos y metodológicos para la integración reflexiva de las TIC e IAGen en el IMSS. Structured Abstract (English) Title: Use of Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) and Its Association with Critical Thinking Dimensions in Higher Education Students: An Explanatory Mixed-Methods Study Background: In the digital era, the ubiquity of Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) and the emergence of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) have reshaped medical learning environments. During Undergraduate Rotating Internship, medical interns face continuous information overload (infoxication) and interaction with automated tools. A purely instrumental or delegative use of ICT may hinder high-order cognitive development, whereas epistemic use can foster clinical analysis, inference, evaluation, and self-regulation. Objective: To determine the association between ICT usage patterns (including GenAI and information literacy) and the development level of critical thinking dimensions in Undergraduate Medical Interns (MIP) across second-level IMSS hospitals, and to interpret underlying metacognitive processes from the students' perspective. Material and Methods: A mixed-methods study with an Explanatory Sequential Design (DEXPLI). · Phase 1 (Quantitative): Multicenter, observational, cross-sectional, analytical study across three sites (General Zone Hospital No. 53, No. 197, and No. 71, OOAD Estado de México Oriente). Total population sampling of active interns will be conducted. Instruments: Multidimensional ICT Usage Patterns Scale (\alpha = 0.87) and a standardized Critical Thinking Dimensions Scale (Facione). Statistical analysis: descriptive metrics, Pearson correlation, multicenter ANOVA, and Multiple Linear Regression models. · Phase 2 (Qualitative): Interpretive phenomenological approach using 4 focus groups (n = 32 interns) selected via purposive extreme-case sampling based on Phase 1 performance quartiles (Q_1 and Q_4). Focus group transcripts will undergo thematic analysis and matrix coding using ATLAS.ti to build integrated meta-inferences. Expected Results: We expect to demonstrate a statistically significant positive association between epistemic ICT/GenAI usage and higher scores in analysis, inference, and self-regulation. Additionally, qualitative analysis will elucidate how passive cognitive delegation links to lower critical performance and how information literacy buffers infoxication during clinical decision-making. Conclusions: This study will provide key empirical evidence to optimize techno-pedagogical curricula for medical internships, informing institutional policies and ethical guidelines for the reflective integration of ICT and GenAI within IMSS training programs. items.title: 360° MDL: The Multidimensional Literature Review Model — Version 2026
items.abstract: 360° MDL (the Multidimensional Literature Review Model) is a methodology for conducting and reporting literature reviews that create value, not just volume. It tells researchers where to look (five evidence stream families: academic databases, influential scholars, industry practice, policy and global organisations, and emerging and diverse voices), what to keep (the 6R Quality Gate and CCD Curation for Complementarity, Coverage and Diversity), how to analyse (eight standard analysis matrices, M1–M8), how sure to be (Triangulation Strength, Resilience Index and a Leave-One-Stream-Out test) and what value to create (Interpretation & Exploitation and an evidence-traced Value-Based Framework). The methodology comes in three tiers: Lite for doctoral students and thesis chapters, Standard for journal review articles, and Advanced for flagship and policy reviews. All three share the 3 × 3 Rule: at least three source streams × at least three analysis matrices. It includes a 30-item reporting checklist (MDL-RC 2026) and a flow diagram compatible with PRISMA 2020, so it complements PRISMA rather than replacing it. This release contains:• Methodology Overview: the full description of the method• Researcher Handbook: step-by-step guidelines, rubrics, checklists and a protocol template• Quick Start Guide and one-page Quick Reference Card: a ready-to-use route in 10 steps for researchers and doctoral students• Excel Toolkit (blank and a worked example) with live calculation of all indices• 24 figures (PNG and vector PDF) and an illustrative example review on smart cities About the author: Professor Miltiadis D. Lytras is Full Professor of Information Systems and Digital Transformation at Deree, The American University of Greece, and Research Professor at Effat University, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. He holds a BSc in Informatics, an MBA and a PhD in Knowledge Management and e-Learning from the Athens University of Economics and Business. His research spans knowledge management, data science, artificial intelligence, the semantic web, technology-enhanced learning and digital transformation. He has served as Editor-in-Chief of the International Journal on Semantic Web and Information Systems, has guest-edited more than 85 special issues in Web of Science-indexed journals, and has authored or edited more than 80 international books. He has been listed among the world's top computer scientists by Guide2Research and among leading scientists in the AD Scientific Index, and he has served as Distinguished Scientist at King Abdulaziz University, Jeddah. 360° MDL distils more than two decades of his experience in editing, reviewing and writing literature reviews into an open, citable methodology. How to cite: Lytras, M. D. (2026). 360° MDL: The Multidimensional Literature Review Model — Version 2026. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23724393 Researchers who use the methodology are invited to state in their methods section: "This review was conducted and reported according to the 360° MDL methodology, Version 2026 (Lytras, 2026)."

items.title: A 4D reconstruction of ancient Troy with AI-assisted interpretive interaction
items.abstract: This paper presents a phase-based, real-time four-dimensional (4D) reconstruction of ancient Troy, enhanced by artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted interpretive interaction with selected virtual characters. Defined by nine superimposed settlement layers, Troy presents particular challenges for conventional two-dimensional (2D) documentation and static three-dimensional (3D) representations, especially when communicating long-term urban transformation to specialist and non-specialist audiences. To address this challenge, all nine principal phases were reconstructed as spatially aligned but separately managed layers within a single Unreal Engine 5 environment. Excavation records, stratigraphic documentation, published archaeological interpretations, and architectural reference drawings were converted into evidence-based 3D models in Autodesk 3ds Max and optimized for real-time visualization. The interpretive component uses retrieval-grounded generative conversational AI, implemented through Convai, for selected phase-aware non-player characters (NPCs). Each character is linked to curated, phase-specific historical knowledge and constrained by a defined speaking scope, contextual prompts, and response rules. The AI was not used to generate archaeological geometry, determine architectural form, or create unrestricted historical narratives. Instead, it supports contextual explanation, visitor orientation, educational mediation, and phase-specific readability while remaining subordinate to the archaeological evidence. The workflow also separates documented, inferred, and speculative elements so that uncertainty can be communicated without presenting every visual decision as equally certain. The project demonstrates that a phase-based real-time environment, combined with carefully bounded conversational AI and virtual reality (VR) interaction, can improve comparative understanding of a multi-layer archaeological site while maintaining archaeological traceability, technical performance, and interpretative transparency. Furthermore, the proposed workflow establishes a reproducible framework for integrating archaeological documentation, immersive visualization, and AI-assisted interpretation within a single interactive environment. By allowing users to examine each settlement phase independently while preserving their spatial correspondence, the system facilitates clearer observation of architectural continuity and transformation over time while supporting transparent scholarly communication, heritage education, future comparative research, and informed public engagement.

items.title: A Comprehensive Review of Transfer Learning-Based Sentiment Analysis Using BERT and Transformer Models
items.abstract: Sentiment analysis is a task in Natural Language Processing (NLP) that detects polarity, opinions, emotions, or attitudes in text data. Traditional systems based on lexicons and hand-crafted features are relatively straightforward, but their adaptability is constrained by vocabulary, context, domain differences, and linguistic variation. Deep learning introduced CNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, GRU, and attention-based representations, while transformer-based pre-trained language models significantly improved contextual transfer. Transfer learning reduces the cost of target-domain annotation by leveraging knowledge from a source domain or a pre-trained model for a target sentiment task. This review examines transfer-learning methods for sentiment analysis, focusing on machine learning, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, Hugging Face Transformers, BERT, and the fine-tuning of pre-trained language models. The literature is organized into transfer-learning taxonomy, model development, BERT-based modifications, hybrid architectures, datasets, evaluation approaches, limitations, and emerging parameter-efficient techniques. The analysis highlights research gaps in source-domain selection, negative-transfer detection, low-resource and code-mixed evaluation, computational efficiency, explainability, continual adaptation, and reproducibility. The review suggests that promising future systems should not focus solely on increasing model size, but should identify relevant knowledge, adapt effectively, and maintain robustness across diverse domains and languages.

items.title: A Conceptual Research on Responsible Artificial Intelligence and Ethical Business Practices
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is becoming part of routine business judgment. Firms use it to identify customers, screen job applicants, anticipate demand, evaluate credit and prepare managerial reports. These applications promise speed and scale. They also create difficult questions about fairness, privacy, worker dignity, accountability and the public consequences of automated decisions. This conceptual paper examines how responsible artificial intelligence can be translated into ethical business practices rather than treated as a separate compliance exercise. Drawing on recent peer-reviewed research published primarily between 2024 and 2026, the discussion connects stakeholder responsibility, organizational governance and the practical management of AI systems. It identifies six business-facing ethical obligations and develops a proposed framework linking leadership commitment, risk-sensitive design, human oversight, stakeholder voice and continuing assurance to ethical outcomes. The paper argues that a responsible firm does more than publish AI principles. It determines where AI should be used, records who remains answerable for each decision and creates a workable route for challenge and correction. The framework is presented as a set of conceptual propositions for subsequent empirical testing. Implications are discussed for managers, auditors, policymakers and smaller firms with limited technical capacity. The central conclusion is that responsible AI is best understood as an ongoing organizational capability that protects human interests while enabling legitimate business innovation

items.title: A Declaration on Power, Freedom, and the Public Nature of Intelligence in the Age of AI
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) evolves into a foundational infrastructure of future civilization, concerns surrounding AI governance extend beyond technological capability and existential risk. This declaration argues that the defining challenge of the AI era lies in the potential concentration of intelligence infrastructure and the resulting concentration of cognitive influence within a limited number of technological ecosystems. While vertically integrated AI systems may accelerate innovation, they may also create new forms of structural dependence that threaten individual and societal freedom. To address these emerging risks, the paper introduces three interrelated concepts: Technological Sovereignty, defined as freedom from dependence on a single technological ecosystem; Cognitive Sovereignty, understood as the ability to maintain meaningful control over one's own processes of thought and judgment; and Ontological Autonomy, the capacity to remain the author of one's own existence in an increasingly AI-mediated world. Building upon the framework of On-Site Adaptive Innovation (OAI), the declaration emphasizes the importance of decentralized adaptive capabilities and the democratization of intelligence infrastructure. It concludes that the future of AI will be shaped not only by the power of intelligent systems but also by the governance structures that determine access to and control of intelligence itself. Preserving technological plurality, cognitive freedom, and human autonomy is therefore presented as a fundamental prerequisite for maintaining freedom in the age of artificial intelligence.

items.title: A Deep Learning and Digital Twin Framework for Automated Crack Detection and Maintenance-Oriented Condition Assessment of Industrial Buildings
items.abstract: The maintenance of industrial buildings is essential to ensure the operability, safety, and efficiency of these facilities, which are key pillars of the industrial sector. Proper maintenance management has a direct impact on productivity and the continuity of operational processes. However, managing the maintenance of these built assets pose significant challenges, particularly in terms of efficiency in inspection, diagnosis, and the planning of corrective and preventive activities, requiring substantial investment to preserve functionality and prevent disruptions. To address these challenges, this paper presents the development of an intelligent system for advanced damage diagnosis in industrial buildings. The system integrates the MIVES multi-criteria decision-making methodology to objectively assess the structural condition of built assets, incorporating complementary technologies: drones for inspection; artificial intelligence (AI) for data analysis and automatic damage detection; extended reality (XR) for the relocalisation of previously captured environments and the spatial positioning of identified damage; and radiance fields (such as 3D Gaussian Splatting) for 3D scene reconstruction and digital twin generation. A prototype workflow for damage detection was developed by training deep-learning algorithms trained on field images of pathologies in industrial built assets and generating digital twins of the facility using photogrammetry techniques and 3D Gaussian Splatting. This workflow supports the detection and visualization of potential pathologies and provides the data necessary for their objective assessment within the MIVES-base condition condition-assessment framework. These developments are integrated into an application that allows managers and asset owners to access and track inspection information through structured damage records, spatial localization, and digital visualization tools that support maintenance planning and decision-making.

items.title: A Framework for Identifying and Understanding Cognitive Biases in Artificial Intelligence–Assisted Radiology
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) creates new susceptibility to diagnostic error in radiology related to the cognitive processes by which radiologists' interpretations incorporate AI outputs. This Perspective presents a conceptual framework for cognitive biases in AI-assisted radiology linking specific biases to radiologist-AI interactions. The framework uses dual-process theory, recognizing fast intuitive and deliberate analytic modes of information processing, as an organizing model for understanding cognitive processes underlying radiologists' decisions and their potential contribution to bias. Across seven decision scenarios spanning image viewing, findings interpretation, and contextual integration, the framework examines how AI output timing, radiologist-AI agreement, trust calibration, and reader expertise influence decision-making. We identify adaptive heuristics that support efficient decisions but, when misapplied or overrelied upon, increase susceptibility to complacency, confirmation, automation, distrust, anchoring, and usual implication bias, and increase behavioral risk of use without qualification. We highlight AI paradoxes emerging from the framework of despecialization, system fragility, and deskilling. Finally, we propose strategies targeting these cognitive biases, including education and experiential learning, workflow and interface design, clinical oversight, and performance monitoring. This framework provides a structured basis for generating testable hypotheses and designing AI-assisted radiology systems that preserve the strengths of human expertise and AI while supporting calibrated reliance.

items.title: A generalizable 3D dose prediction across heterogeneous cohorts: A framework developed for the 2025 AAPM GDP‐HMM challenge
items.abstract: Abstract Background Manual radiotherapy treatment planning is labor‐intensive, subjective, and highly variable across planners and institutions. Deep learning has emerged as a promising approach for estimating achievable three‐dimensional (3D) dose distributions for a given plan (hereafter: dose prediction) by directly mapping patient anatomy and beam geometry to voxel‐wise dose. However, achieving robust generalization across diverse anatomical sites, prescriptions, and institutions remains a major challenge, particularly under computational constraints required for clinical deployment. Purpose We sought to develop and evaluate a generalizable, computationally efficient 3D dose prediction framework capable of spanning heterogeneous multi‐site and multi‐cohort datasets, as defined in the 2025 AAPM Generalizable Dose Prediction for Heterogeneous Multi‐Cohort and Multi‐Site (GDP‐HMM) Grand Challenge. Our goal was to design a model that not only achieved state‐of‐the‐art voxel‐wise accuracy but also maintained clinically meaningful dose‐volume and geometric characteristics across diverse cases. Methods We implemented a fully convolutional 3D dose‐prediction model adapted from the MedNeXt architecture, which was originally introduced as a high‐capacity convolutional backbone for medical image segmentation and is well suited to volumetric dense prediction tasks. The network accepted multimodal inputs comprising CT, PTV/OAR masks, beam and angle plates, and scalar plan metadata. A composite loss function combined voxel‐wise L 1 , body‐masked weighted L 1 , structure‐wise moment‐matching, and gradient‐based penalties to jointly preserve spatial fidelity and dosimetric accuracy. The model was trained on the fixed GDP‐HMM dataset consisting of 2876 training plans, 356 validation plans, and a held‐out test set of 498 plans using random 3D patches and evaluated by mean absolute error (MAE), homogeneity index (HI), and conformity indices (CI100%, CI50%). Ablation studies quantified the contribution of each loss component to overall performance. Statistical comparisons used paired Wilcoxon tests with false discovery rate correction. Results The proposed model achieved a mean voxel‐wise MAE of 2.04 Gy on the validation set, outperforming the challenge baseline (2.54 Gy). An ensemble with the baseline further improved MAE to 1.94 Gy on the validation set and 2.071 Gy on the held‐out test set, corresponding to the lowest test‐set MAE and first‐place overall ranking in the GDP‐HMM Challenge. Predicted dose distributions preserved key plan characteristics, with ΔHI, ΔCI 100% , and ΔCI 50% narrowly centered around zero, indicating consistent target coverage and dose conformity. Protocol‐specific evaluations for head‐and‐neck and lung cohorts demonstrated close alignment with reference plans, with no systematic degradation in OAR endpoints. Ablation experiments showed that removing gradient‐based terms increased MAE by 0.50 Gy, while excluding the moment‐matching term increased MAE by 0.06 Gy confirming that both gradient‐ and moment‐based constraints enhanced spatial and dosimetric fidelity. Conclusion We present a generalizable 3D dose prediction framework that achieves state‐of‐the‐art accuracy while satisfying stringent runtime requirements (< 3s per case on < 24 GB GPU memory). By integrating gradient‐aware and moment‐based constraints within a MedNeXt backbone, the model preserved clinical DVH endpoints and geometric plan features. These findings demonstrate that carefully engineered loss formulations are pivotal for cross‐institutional generalization. The framework offers a foundation for rapid dose prediction that could accelerate treatment planning, reduce inter‐planner variability, and enable intelligent automation in radiotherapy workflows.

items.title: A Human-Stiffness-Based Simulator for Ergonomic Evaluation of Pistol-Grip Power Tool Reaction
items.abstract: Powered pistol-grip fastening tools can produce substantial handle rotation during torque build-up, which may contribute to operator overuse injuries. This study developed and evaluated a human-stiffness-based physical simulator for a controlled relative comparison of fastening variables affecting peak handle rotation. The simulator used a DC-powered pistol-grip tool, which was constrained to rotate about its spindle axis, with a double-acting pneumatic cylinder providing resistance set according to a specified human-derived stiffness. The evaluation used stiffness data from 10 operators at 5 and 7.5 N·m, with simulator peak displacement compared to in vivo measurements using paired analyses. The simulator was then used as a screening platform to examine the effect of target torque and, at 7.5 N·m, the effects of fastener material, drive style, head type, and spindle speed. The simulator overpredicted human peak displacement, with mean biases of 14.72° at 5 N·m and 10.29° at 7.5 N·m. The peak rotation increased by 15.0% when torque was increased from 5 to 7.5 N·m (p = 0.022). Torx Plus style fasteners produced 11.5% less rotation than Hex drive fasteners; fastener material significantly affected rotation; head type did not; and rotation was substantially lower at 160 rpm. Although the simulator did not reproduce absolute human displacement without bias, the results support its use as a screening platform for relative comparison under fixed mechanical boundary conditions rather than as an absolute predictor of human displacement or injury risk.

items.title: A Landscape Review of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Enabled Teacher Professional Development at Scale
items.abstract: Teacher Professional Development (TPD) significantly influences student learning, yet implementing equitable, quality, and efficient TPD at scale remains a persistent challenge. Emerging technologies—particularly Artificial Intelligence (AI)—offer promising avenues for addressing tensions between localisation and personalisation, but a comprehensive understanding of AI’s role in scaling in-service TPD remains lacking. Guided by the overarching question of how AI enables in-service TPD to be implemented at scale with equity, quality, and efficiency, this landscape review examines three research questions: how AI-enabled TPD programmes address equity, quality, and efficiency at scale; what roles AI plays in enabling TPD at scale; and what promising practices and lessons emerge from such programmes. The review draws conceptually on the World Bank Group’s Technology for Teaching (T4T) framework, which delineates three sequential stages of technology-enhanced TPD: Access, Engage, and Apply. Sources included peer-reviewed studies, policy documents, and grey literature with a pre-defined typology. From an initial pool of 576 articles, 504 were screened after removing duplicates; 34 articles directly addressing the research questions underwent full-text review, supplemented by 59 partially aligned sources. Findings indicate that AI-enabled TPDs address equity, quality, and efficiency at scale by expanding equitable access for teachers of less mainstream K-12 subjects and geographically distant populations while supporting teacher retention by fostering meaningful learning and reducing administrative burden. Regarding roles that AI plays in enabling TPD at scale, AI’s principal affordances include expanding teachers’ knowledge base and learning assets, functioning as a personalised learning coach, and supporting classroom learning management beyond the TPD itself. Common practices that are tentatively effective emerged from the findings include AI chatbots, AI-assisted evaluation reports, and AI-enabled automation, with strong AI-capable leadership emerging as a potentially critical enabler. This review paper also provided practical implications for TPD practitioners, as well as directions for future research. items.title: A Large Language Model–Guided Q‐Learning Method for Food Safety Sampling Decision‐Making
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Food safety sampling is a critical measure for safeguarding public health; however, current regulatory practices are challenged by fragmented risk signals, constrained inspection resources, and suboptimal inspection efficiency. To address these issues, this paper proposes a food safety sampling decision‐making method based on large language models (LLM)–guided Q‐learning. First, we leverage LLMs to extract and analyze key elements from unstructured online food safety public opinion data. This is integrated with clustering analysis and the entropy weight method to achieve quantitative risk assessment and grading. Subsequently, a food category–region risk score matrix is constructed, and the allocation of sampling frequency is formalized as a sequential decision‐making problem under resource constraints. Q‐learning is then introduced to learn optimal sampling strategies, using LLM‐generated structured heuristic values as prior guidance, thereby reducing ineffective exploration and enhancing training efficiency. Experimental results, based on data from 30 provincial administrative regions, 457 municipalities/counties, and 25 food categories, generated 4690 risk evaluation records as effective inputs for decision‐making. The results demonstrate that the derived sampling strategies align with risk priors, allocating higher sampling intensity to high‐risk food category–region combinations while maintaining coverage balance across food categories and regions. Compared to the baseline without heuristic guidance, LLM guidance significantly reduces convergence iterations while maintaining steady‐state rewards. This indicates that the proposed method accelerates policy learning without compromising long‐term returns. In conclusion, this study validates that the proposed method achieves a closed‐loop integration of risk assessment and decision optimization, providing a data‐driven methodology for intelligent food safety regulation.

items.title: A model for enhancing the quality of geography education based on the integration of Artificial Intelligence and Geographic Information Systems
items.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) is increasingly central to improving the quality of geography education. This study developed a model intended for enhancing geography education quality based on AI-GIS integration and empirically examined future geography teachers’ readiness to adopt these technologies, drawing on a survey of 100 bachelor's, master's, and doctoral students in geography at al-Farabi Kazakh National University (27 items across three blocks: socio-intellectual characteristics, experience and integration, and professional/ethical issues; Cronbach's α = 0.78, χ 2 (3) = 24.56, p < 0.001). Sixty-seven percent of students reported readiness to use AI-GIS technologies (12% fully ready, 55% ready but requiring further training), and an equal share wished to develop their knowledge in this area further; familiarity was higher for AI (68%) than for GIS (26%) or GeoAI (8%); 99% had used ChatGPT or a similar tool, and ArcGIS was the most common GIS platform (66%). Readiness to use the technologies was associated with GIS familiarity ( ρ = 0.51), GIS proficiency ( ρ = 0.47), and GeoAI knowledge ( ρ = 0.43), but not with general AI familiarity ( ρ = 0.07); H3 and H4 were supported, H1 was not, and H2 was reported as a descriptive result. Although 88% of students viewed AI-GIS integration as beneficial to instructional quality, 67% were unaware of algorithmic bias issues and only 6% had applied these technologies in teaching practice. The results informed a proposed five-component model (content, technological, methodological, integrative, and competency) that has not yet been tested empirically. It is intended for improving teacher-training programs, designing practical courses, and developing future teachers’ digital competence, critical thinking, and ethical awareness.

items.title: A Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Dynamic Constitutional (Prakriti) Profiling and Personalized Ayurvedic Interventions
items.abstract: Traditional Ayurvedic diagnostics rely on determining an individual's baseline constitution (Prakriti) and acute functional imbalances (Vikriti) through qualitative clinical evaluations and longitudinal lifestyle assessments. While foundational to personalized holistic care, manual constitutional profiling exhibits inter-practitioner variability, requires substantial clinical time, and lacks continuous adaptability to acute physiological or environmental shifts. This paper presents a Multi-Agent Large Language Model (LLM) and Rule-Hybrid Architecture designed to structure constitutional classification and generate source-grounded lifestyle (Vihara), dietary (Ahara), and botanical (Aushadha) educational recommendations. By decoupling diagnostic sub-tasks across specialized cooperative agents and enforcing a deterministic rule-verification engine, the proposed framework separates stable baseline traits from transient symptom fluctuations while constraining unsupported generative outputs. Evaluated on a held-out synthetic benchmark cohort of 200 multi-modal profiles (derived from a 250-profile curated dataset) labeled by a consensus panel of three certified Ayurvedic physicians, the framework achieves an overall classification accuracy of 90.0%, a macro-F1 score of 0.892, and a system-to-consensus Cohen's kappa of κ=0.863(95% CI: 0.808–0.918). Ablation experiments against deterministic rule baselines and monolithic single-LLM configurations demonstrate that multi-agent task separation combined with deterministic safety gating eliminates 100.0% of predefined contraindication rule violations across benchmark and adversarial stress tests. Adhering to TRIPOD+AI reporting standards, we detail the knowledge-base provenance, system failure modes, computational overhead, and human-in-the-loop governance required for responsible deployment in integrative health informatics. items.title: A Pedagogical Framework Based on Design Dissection to Drive Innovation in Technically Complex Product Design Education
items.abstract: Designing innovative products integrated with technically complex product de- sign focused on user centric remains a significant challenges in design education. Product dissec- tion has been utilized as one of the efficient methods to interact the products to understand its working principle and to generate creative outcomes. The proposed pedagogical framework focus mainly on the functional understanding of the product being dissected. The purpose of the pro- posed work is to investigate the effectiveness of the students learning rate with respect to the product types such as mechanical, and electrical. The approach of the investigation deals with the design dissection of various products as a core teaching methods. The application of particular design thinking methods such as SCAMPER, and Morphological Matrix as blend with design dissection increase the creative outcomes. Technical realizability, ergonomic, user experience, compliance with standard and novelty are the metrics to evaluate the design outcomes. Better understanding of the various domain principles of components with functional complexities leads to innovative concepts and new product design. The findings from this investigation expose the understanding of products through the design dissection and the effectiveness in the creative design.

items.title: A Physics-Informed Surrogate Safety Gate for Agentic AI Control of SMT Reflow Soldering in Unmanned-System Electronics Manufacturing: A Simulation-Based Study
items.abstract: Surface mount technology (SMT) assembly lines running under high-mix low-volume (HMLV) conditions face a recurring parameter-optimization problem, because frequent product changeovers invalidate static control recipes and expose the nonlinear coupling between solder paste printing and reflow soldering. A large language model (LLM) can reason about that coupling. Its outputs are probabilistic and its inference latency is network-dependent, so it cannot be wired directly to process actuators. This paper takes that obstacle as its research question. The proposed multilayer Agentic AI and physics-informed digital twin (Agentic AI-DT) framework, a digital-twin architecture evaluated here as a digital model driven by a simulated closed loop, places a cloud-hosted LLM in the strategy role and an edge-deployed conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE), trained with a thermodynamic partial differential equation residual penalty, in the role of a gate that runs the same deterministic check on every strategy before it reaches the reflow oven controller. The check executes deterministically, but its verdicts inherit the surrogate's prediction error, so the safety it provides is measured here and not assumed. The study measures the gate itself: how often it fires, and how often it errs in each direction. A two-stage pipeline combining Latin Hypercube Sampling with singular value decomposition based reduced-order modelling expands 1,000 calibrated finite element simulations into 50,000 training scenarios, and 200 further independent finite element runs form the held-out test set. On those runs the physics-informed CVAE reaches a mean squared error of 1.93 ℃ 2 , 25.2% below a CVAE trained without the physics term and 14.6% below a standalone physics-informed neural network. Across 347 candidate strategies the gate vetoes 63 (18.2%). Finite element re-simulation shows that 5 of the 284 admitted candidates (1.76%, 95% CI 0.8 to 4.1%) were unsafe and that 14 of the 63 vetoed candidates (22.2%, 95% CI 13.7 to 33.9%) were safe, giving 94.5% agreement with the reference solver. Closed-loop profile tracking error is 2.09 ℃, against 3.18 ℃ for model predictive control and 4.62 ℃ for fixed-gain PID. The diagnostic layer names the injected root cause in 84.0% of 300 scripted fault trials, against 72.7% for a random forest classifier and 61.3% for a rule-based expert system. Median end-to-end latency is 419 ms, 90.7% of 2,000 cycles finish inside the 500 ms design budget, and the remaining cycles commit a re-checked last validated setpoint at the 500 ms boundary, reaching the controller within 539 ms. Every number reported here comes from a synthetic environment calibrated against three published sets of measured reflow profiles. No physical production line was instrumented, so these are simulation-fidelity measurements rather than production performance guarantees.

items.title: A proposed HTTPS Like Security Layer for AI agent actions: it asks "will this action do exactly what it was authorized to do?"
items.abstract: The internet already has strong answers for many security questions. TCP/IP delivers data. HTTPS and TLS encrypt the connection and confirm the server’s identity. OAuth grants an application access to an account. Identity systems confirm who a user or workload is. Logs and monitoring record what happened afterwards. Each of these remains essential, and each answers a question about the connection, the identity, or the record. AI agents raise a different question. An agent can now call APIs, send emails, export files, initiate payments, change databases, reconfigure cloud infrastructure, issue network commands, and control physical devices, often in milliseconds and without a human in the loop. A request can travel over a perfectly secure HTTPS connection, carry a valid OAuth token, and come from an authenticated agent, yet carry the wrong amount, the wrong destination, an expired approval, a revoked permission, a replayed request, or an instruction injected into the agent through a malicious prompt. By the time monitoring raises an alert, the payment has settled, the data has left, and the system has changed. This disclosure proposes a security layer above HTTPS that verifies each action at the moment it takes effect. Every action an AI agent proposes is held in a pending state with no external effect. A protected component, outside the agent’s control, checks that specific action against the conditions that apply: who authorized it, for what purpose, to which destination, under which policy version, within which time window, and whether permission has since been revoked. When every check passes, it issues a single-use authorization bound to that exact action and to the specific system that will carry it out. That system, whether an API gateway, payment processor, cloud control plane, network egress gateway, database, or device controller, verifies the authorization and consumes it in the same step as execution. An altered, replayed, expired, or unverified action stays blocked, and alternate routes to the same effect, such as backup systems, debug interfaces, or direct device access, pass through the same check. The layer works alongside HTTPS, OAuth, identity management, and existing access controls, and requires none of them to change. It applies to AI agents and tool calls, cloud operations, payments, telecommunications, and critical infrastructure. HTTPS secures the connection; this layer ensures each action does exactly what it was authorized to do. items.title: A Relational Framework for Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Shared Decision Making
items.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) can support clinical decision making, but accuracy, usability, and efficiency do not establish whether patients understand options or influence the agreed plan. This study aimed to develop observable relational requirements for AI-assisted shared decision making. Methods: We conducted a qualitative framework synthesis of 21 clinical, empirical, conceptual, and governance sources identified through structured purposive sampling completed on 20 September 2026. Two-pass coding combined established shared decision-making categories with inductive analysis of AI-related relational effects. Domains were retained when supported across source types, conceptually distinct, observable at the point of care, and linked to a clinical or organizational response. Results: The synthesis identified a patient–clinician–AI interaction embedded in organizational governance and highlighted five relational concerns: apparent authority of AI output, insufficient verification and contestability, substitution of inferred for expressed preferences, uncertainty without actionable follow-up, and fragmented responsibility. These concerns informed five domains: role and influence disclosure; independent verification and contestability; direct preference elicitation; actionable uncertainty and revisability; and distributed accountability and continuity. Each domain was translated into a relational question, a clinical test, and a documentation or governance response. A complementary measurement framework distinguished technical performance from decision process, relational quality, equity, safety and continuity, and governance outcomes. Conclusions: The study’s contribution is an operational framework connecting AI-related relational concerns to observable clinical requirements and candidate evaluation measures. The proposed framework requires stakeholder and prospective clinical validation; it does not establish clinical effectiveness.

items.title: A Resource- and Power-Efficient FPGA Implementation of a Segmented Chebyshev Tanh Activation Function Using Single-Precision Floating-Point Arithmetic
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence and machine learning workloads increasingly rely on dedicated hardware accelerators, including field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), which offer parallelism and reconfigurability. The hyperbolic tangent (tanh) is widely used as a nonlinear activation function yet is costly to evaluate directly in hardware, making efficient approximation essential. This work presents an FPGA implementation of a segmented Chebyshev-polynomial-based tanh core for IEEE-754 single-precision floating-point. The input domain x∈[−6,6] is reduced to |x|∈[0,6] by exploiting tanh’s odd symmetry, and partitioned into three sub-intervals with per-interval Chebyshev degrees selected to achieve the target accuracy. Polynomial evaluation is performed via Clenshaw’s recurrence, with a single recurrence stage reused for all evaluation steps under finite-state-machine control. Implemented and verified on an Altera Cyclone V FPGA, the core uses 1176 adaptive logic modules, 317 registers, and one digital signal processing (DSP) block. It requires 28 clock cycles for inputs within the approximation domain and 3 outside it, and dissipates 6.20 mW of dynamic power at 40 MHz. The mean absolute error is 8.26×10−8 across the tested inputs and 5.74×10−8 over a denser MATLAB sweep. Against exponential-based, continued-fraction-based, and polynomial-based tanh approximations, it achieves the lowest register, DSP, memory, and dynamic power utilization.

items.title: A Review of AI-Based Job Portal Systems for Intelligent Job Matching and Recruitment
items.abstract: The growth of digital recruitment has created large volumes of job postings, candidate profiles, resumes, applications, and interaction data. Conventional job portals mainly support job publication, keyword search, filtering, application submission, and employer-side candidate management. Although these functions improve access to employment opportunities, they do not always solve the core matching problem: identifying the most relevant job for a candidate and the most suitable candidate for an employer. Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Natural Language Processing (NLP), and recommender-system techniques provide opportunities to improve this process by understanding skills, experience, qualifications, job descriptions, preferences, and historical interactions. This review paper examines research on job recommender systems, e-recruitment recommendation, semantic job matching, resume screening, deep-learning-based talent recommendation, and algorithmic fairness. The literature indicates a progression from content-based and collaborative filtering toward hybrid, semantic, and deep-learning approaches. Recent studies further emphasize explainability, fairness, semantic embeddings, and large-language-model-assisted recruitment. Based on the reviewed literature, this paper proposes an AI-enabled job portal architecture combining a React Native mobile client, Spring Boot backend, MySQL database, and Python-based AI services. The proposed architecture supports role-based access for job seekers, employers, and administrators; resume processing; skill extraction; semantic candidate-job matching; personalized job recommendations; application tracking; employer notifications; and chatbot assistance. The paper identifies major research gaps involving cold-start users, limited public recruitment datasets, explainability, fairness, dynamic job preferences, and integration of multiple recruitment functions into a practical end-to-end platform. Finally, evaluation metrics and an experimental methodology are proposed for assessing recommendation quality, classification performance, response time, usability, and fairness.

items.title: A Review of Machine Learning Approaches to Eye Disease Detection: Current Trends, Challenges and Future Directions
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Vision impairment and blindness remain a major global health challenge, with glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, age-related macular degeneration, cataract, corneal disease, and retinopathy of prematurity representing important causes of preventable or treatable vision loss when detected early. This clinical need has accelerated research on machine learning approaches for automatic detection of eye diseases, grading, and segmentation. However, existing reviews often focus on a single disease or method. They also give limited attention to their suitability and applicability for reliable clinical deployments. This review synthesizes traditional machine learning, deep learning, vision transformers, ensemble and hybrid models, segmentation methods, and explainable AI approaches for eye disease detection. It further examines task formulation, dataset characteristics, evaluation practices, and deployment constraints, with emphasis on clinical readiness rather than benchmark performance alone. Methods: A structured narrative review was conducted using recently published articles from reputable databases and repositories, including IEEE Xplore, PubMed/MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, Scopus and arXiv. The review critically analyzes the progression from traditional machine learning to advanced models, including deep learning, vision transformers, ensemble models and explainable artificial intelligence. Studies were critically analyzed according to task formulations, dataset characteristics, segmentation approaches, evaluation metrics, explainability, and deployment constraints. Results: The synthesis shows that class imbalance, limited demographic and geographic diversity in available datasets, weak external validation, and scarce prospective evidence continue to separate benchmark performance from clinical readiness. Explainability is also often evaluated through visual plausibility rather than validated faithfulness. Currently, data-driven diabetic retinopathy screening is closest to clinical readiness, particularly for distinguishing referable from non-referable cases, whereas multi-label detection, rare disease detection, and cross-device deployment remain at the research stage. Conclusions: Progress towards clinical adoption requires stronger alignment between experimental evaluation and real-world deployment. This includes external validation and the development of equitable, interpretable, and resource-aware systems.

items.title: A Review of Machine Learning Techniques for Analog-To-Digital Converter Design Automation
items.abstract: ADCs play an important role in converting information from the analog world to the digital one; with modern applications requiring higher resolutions, speed, and power efficiency, it has become very difficult to design them. Traditionally, the design of an ADC follows an iterative design process that includes stages like specification, behavioral modeling, transistor sizing, schematic simulation, layout, and post-layout verification, which is laborious and requires much designer expertise due to the consideration of process-voltage-temperature variations and yield. In this work, we perform a review of the latest advancements in the use of machine learning (ML) to tackle the challenges of ADC design in recent years, with systematic search from 2015 to 2026 in IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and arXiv. Rather than organizing the literature on different ML algorithms, this paper categorizes ML approaches such as regression, tree-based models, SVM, ANN, CNN, GNN, reinforcement learning, evolutionary algorithms, and Bayesian optimization in ADC design stages such as behavioral modeling, transistor sizing, calibration of comparators and capacitor arrays, calibration of ADC, layout optimization, prediction of PVT/yield variations, and design space exploration. Comparative analysis includes the benefits provided by each technique such as speed and accuracy improvements, as well as their main drawbacks. Open challenges are then presented, including lack of data, poor generalization performance, low explainability, and the largely unexplored topic of co-optimization across multiple stages. Finally, future trends in the field are presented in terms of new directions such as generative AI, GNN-based layout optimization, physics-informed learning, digital twins, and human-AI collaborative design, as well as risks and potential problems such as manufacturability and IP in generative approaches

items.title: A Scoping Review of Sentiment Analysis for Customer Satisfaction in Digital Banking: Mapping the Research Gap Toward Multimodal Integration
items.abstract: Sentiment analysis has become increasingly important for interpreting customer-generated content across social media and digital technologies. However, research on digital banking continues to rely predominantly on textonly data, with limited attention to multimodal integration. This scoping review mapped the literature on sentiment analysis for customer satisfaction in digital banking, identified research gaps, and outlined future directions. The review followed the PRISMA-ScR guidelines and searched six databases—ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore, Wiley Online Library, ACM Digital Library, SpringerLink, and Google Scholar—for English-language studies published from 2015 to 2026; the final search was conducted on May 10, 2026. Of 1,631 records identified, 35 studies met the inclusion criteria. Text only data were used in 31 studies (88.6%), multi-source text was used in one study (2.9%), text combined with survey data in two studies (5.7%), and numerical time-series data in one study (2.9%); no included study integrated text, audio, and video within a single sentiment analysis framework. The literature was geographically concentrated and relied mainly on traditional machine-learning and hybrid approaches, whereas transformer/LLM based methods, explainable AI, and real-time approaches remained limited. The absence of banking-specific multimodal datasets is a key barrier to progress. Future research should prioritize privacy-preserving multimodal datasets, multilingual and culturally diverse models, explainable AI, and real-time deployment to support more reliable assessment of customer experience in digital banking.
